exposure: Rupture location (lower-segment scar, non-lower-segment scar, unscarred)
cohort: 30 pregnant women with uterine rupture who delivered at Chang-Gung Memorial Hospital between November 2004 and July 2017
finding: Uterine rupture occurred most often after 30 weeks of gestation and was associated with significant maternal and fetal morbidity, with unscarred uteri rupturing later in gestation and resulting in higher fetal birth weights compared to scarred uteri.
mod_finding: Four ruptures occurred postpartum of vaginal delivery, three after trials of labor after cesarean delivery, and one in an unscarred uterus; two of the four women with postpartum rupture eventually underwent hysterectomy.
gest_age: Mean gestational age at rupture: 34.2 weeks
birth_weight: Higher fetal birth weights were observed in women with unscarred uteri compared to those with scarred uteri
